headline: OpenRAC's desktop launcher lands with disc setup and save-management tools
summary: The desktop launcher lands in #2 and gains disc inspection, setup controls, a level-editor entry and a prototype save manager. Later changes remove PCSX2 launch options, while the proposed native-port architecture in #3 remains unmerged. The launcher is still scaffolding, and its runtime and editor actions are reported as tested from a shell rather than from the desktop app. Master receives direct development work and a history rewrite rather than a release pull request.
highlights: The save panel shows slots, timestamps, planets and bolt counts, with named backups and restoration.
Discord activity, Linux desktop integration and cached progress displays are added, followed by fixes for navigation stalls and progress-sync responses.
A runtime experiment boots Ratchet & Clank PAL and US and Going Commando US into their first levels, with sound and memory-card work. Going Commando's movies are skipped.

The experiment also runs some reconstructed C as host code, but #3 proposes replacing the emulation approach with native-port scaffolding. Neither the proposal nor the launcher establishes a finished native game.
